scope: Proposition 4.11 (Sphere projections) of the manuscript “Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers” (preprints/Abelian-covers-Gale-correspondences-and-the-Hodge-conjecture-for-powers-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 032 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3467c8077855a568), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At every s ∈ T Hg ϕ the following assertions hold. (i) If n ≥ 3, then either Mχ is finite and the Hodge action on its rational scalar orbit is toric, or M◦ χ = ( Sp(Wχ), χ2 = 1, SL(Wχ), χ2 ̸= 1. In the infinite case the derived Hodge projection is the same standard group. (ii) In dimensions at most two every non-toric character space has dimension two and has standard derived Hodge projection SL2. Here the symplectic group is for the restricted polarization on the order-two character space. Each non-toric character space is supported by a single simple ideal of Lie(Jder)k.
